content:
Hi all,

I have been working on a standalone Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization project about determinantal ideals:

https://github.com/WangJiabai/Determinantal-Ideals-Formalization/tree/main

The project formalizes a development around generic minors, determinantal ideals, standard bitableaux, the KRS correspondence, straightening, and the Gröbner-basis theorem for generic determinantal ideals. The final part of the project proves the Gröbner-basis theorem through the standard-bitableau / KRS / Hilbert-function route.

I would like to start upstreaming only a small foundational part to Mathlib, not the full Sturmfels/KRS/Groebner development.

My intended first PR would be a Mathlib-style refactor of the basic API for determinantal ideals of a generic matrix. Tentatively, it would include:

  • an index type for t × t minors, something like Matrix.MinorIndex m n t;
  • minors of the existing generic matrix Matrix.mvPolynomialX (Fin m) (Fin n) R;
  • the finite set of all t × t generic minors;
  • the determinantal ideal generated by these minors;
  • basic membership lemmas;
  • evaluation of generic minors at a concrete matrix;
  • compatibility with coefficient-ring maps / base change;
  • finite generation of the determinantal ideal.

I do not plan to include in the first PR the KRS correspondence, standard bitableaux, straightening law, term orders, or the Gröbner-basis theorem. I also plan to postpone Laplace-expansion lemmas and the theorem that larger minors lie in ideals generated by smaller minors, unless reviewers think those should be included immediately.

I would appreciate advice on two design questions before preparing the PR:

  1. Does this sound like an appropriate first contribution to Mathlib?
  2. Where should the file live? My current guess is something like
    Mathlib/RingTheory/MvPolynomial/DeterminantalIdeal.lean, possibly with the purely matrix-level API split into a separate matrix file if preferred.

Any comments on naming, namespace organization, or PR size would be very helpful.

Hi! Can you comment on whether you've used AI for this project, and (if so), how? This is not forbidden for mathlib, but it influences what kind of feedback we would give you. (Mathlib contribution policy requires disclosing such usage anyway.)

For instance, your repository contained an AGENTS.md file which has been deleted --- so I suppose the answer is some kind of yes. The details matter here.

Michael Rothgang said:

Hi! Can you comment on whether you've used AI for this project, and (if so), how? This is not forbidden for mathlib, but it influences what kind of feedback we would give you. (Mathlib contribution policy requires disclosing such usage anyway.)

For instance, your repository contained an AGENTS.md file which has been deleted --- so I suppose the answer is some kind of yes. The details matter here.

Yes, I used ChatGPT and Codex, and I should have disclosed this more clearly earlier.

The mathematical goal of the project comes from my thesis project. My advisor works in computer algebra and commutative algebra, and I chose the Gröbner basis theory of determinantal ideals as the target. I used ChatGPT early on to discuss feasibility, the overall formalization plan, and possible Lean formulations of the basic definitions and theorem statements.

I also used Codex while developing the Lean code. In particular, after I had decided on theorem and lemma statements and had a mathematical reference or intended proof route, I used Codex to draft proof scripts. I treated the generated code as draft code: I reviewed it, revised it, and rejected or rewrote it when it did not match the mathematical definition or proof structure I wanted.

For example, in the formalization of the width notion in Sturmfels.lean, Codex initially suggested a decomposed auxiliary-definition style. I thought this did not match the definition I wanted from the paper, so I rejected that version, wrote a different definition, and proved the needed properties from it.

About AGENTS.md: it was an instruction file for local coding-agent experiments, not mathematical content. I understand that deleting it may have caused confusion. I deleted it because it did not belong to the mathematical library content, not to hide AI usage.

the determinantal ideal generated by these minors

This sounds like Fitting ideal; is it?

Jz Pan said:

the determinantal ideal generated by these minors

This sounds like Fitting ideal; is it?

I looked up the terminology, and yes, this seems to be a special case of a Fitting ideal. I meant the ideal generated by all t × t minors of the generic m × n matrix with entries X_ij; viewed as a presentation matrix, this gives a Fitting ideal of the corresponding cokernel, up to the usual indexing convention.
I opened the PR and CI passes. I would appreciate comments on the API design, naming, and file location.
